A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FUSER and FUSER-DF. Their text, tables, figures, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching v1's supplementary Sections 6–8 to v2's Appendices A–C.

before.justification: Sections 4.2–4.3 report original registration results, ablations, runtime measurements, and qualitative examples for FUSER and FUSER-DF.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments and ablations, revises their results, and adds experiments on independently captured indoor sequences in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The absolute geometric encoder, 32 alternating attention layers, transferred attention weights, pose regression heads, training losses, and diffusion refinement procedure remain unchanged. The revised scores are not accompanied by a documented algorithm or architecture change.

E1.justification: Appendix D adds self-captured kitchen/living-room and study-room sequences acquired with an iPhone 14 Pro Max. This extends the evaluated indoor data while retaining the four training datasets and three benchmark datasets.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 1–5 and Figure 5 are unchanged, including the ScanNet synchronization methods and the Full/SGHR combinations with point-cloud descriptors. Newly cited related work is not added to these comparisons.

E3.justification: The new phone evaluation uses two 100-view sequences. Section 4.1 also replaces the blanket eight-GPU description with eight-GPU training and single-GPU evaluation, without establishing that experiments were rerun. Existing benchmark sampling, metrics, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D and Figure 7 add qualitative case studies examining registration on self-captured scenes with sparse, distorted, and noisy points. The existing data-volume and attention-prior ablation questions remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Both retain aggregate errors and threshold percentages; additional decimal precision does not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 substantially revise the reported results. ScanNet FUSER Rot@3° changes from 65.2% to 69.4%; ArkitScenes RR changes from 84.1% to 92.1% for FUSER and from 90.3% to 95.0% for FUSER-DF. Changes are not uniformly favorable: Table 2's FUSER-DF rotation error increases from 2.9° to 3.1°. Figure 7 adds qualitative outcomes and approximately 0.38-second runtimes per 100-view sequence.

T1.justification: Equation (9) changes the residual likelihood's conditioning from S_1 to S. Appendix B's corresponding derivation and Equation (19) still condition on S_1, leaving an unexplained mismatch. The remaining mathematical definitions and derivations are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about direct feed-forward multiview registration, transferred 2D attention priors, SE(3)^N diffusion refinement, and accuracy and efficiency advantages.

C2.justification: v2 removes the explicit limitations paragraph acknowledging indoor-only coverage and unexplored model-capacity scaling. Appendix D additionally interprets its qualitative phone examples as evidence of strong robustness and real-world generalizability.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 distinguishes training hardware from single-GPU evaluation, making the execution resources more explicit. Appendix D identifies the capture device and clarifies that textures are used only for visualization, while model inputs contain point-cloud data. The code-access URL and principal hyperparameters are unchanged.

R1.justification: Sections 1–2 add citations and brief coverage of reinforcement-learning and diffusion approaches, including Generative Point Cloud Registration and Diff-Reg. This broadens contextual coverage without substantially changing the paper's positioning against pairwise-then-global registration.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized related-work and experimental-prose edits, corrects affiliations and the ablation heading, adds acknowledgments, and relabels the existing appendices A–C before adding Appendix D. The main exposition and section ordering remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 7 showing the two phone-captured sequences and their registered outputs. Figures 1–6 and Tables 1–5 retain their basic displays; appendix headings, caption references, and text placement receive limited formatting changes.

improvement.justification: The phone case studies and explicit single-GPU evaluation add practical evidence and improve documentation. However, v2 removes useful limitations disclosure and introduces a mismatch between Equations (9) and (19). The extensive benchmark score revisions are unexplained, and higher reported recalls alone do not establish improved paper quality. These benefits and harms do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
